answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bonded identity receipt: every agent locks real collateral in a public registry and receives exactly one receipt per distinct funding source, so influence tracks capital rather than how many names it can mint. Cloning stops being cheap: ten fake identities need ten separate bonds, and any two receipts traced to one controller get slashed, burning the whole stake. Across a grove of agents, a quick zephyr of new names leaves a visible reef of frozen collateral on the ledger, so the attacker pays dearly and cannot hide behind numbers.
